title: The Other Side of the Coin: Exploring Fairness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
findings: The paper found that the effect of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on religious bias is dependent on the scale of the Large Language Model (LLM). For small-scale LLMs (e.g., Llama3.2-1B, Mistral-7B), RAG often exacerbated unfairness by increasing agreement with religious stereotypes. Conversely, for large-scale LLMs (e.g., Llama3 70b, glm-4-plus), the RAG paradigm improved fairness. The proposed mitigation strategies, FairFT and FairFilter, were demonstrated to be effective in reducing this religious bias for small-scale models.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the model's agreement percentage on stereotypical sentences related to religion, as part of a broader fairness evaluation. A lower agreement percentage on stereotypes indicates better fairness.
